text:
Boston won 6-3, but the numbers say San Jose played the game almost even. The Sharks deserved to win 47 percent of the time, against 53 for the Bruins, and at even strength the two teams created nearly identical chances (2.24 expected goals for San Jose, 2.21 for Boston). The gap came from special teams and a late pile-on, not from one side controlling play. San Jose also outshot Boston 38 to 26 and put up 65 shot attempts to the Bruins' 50, though Boston blocked 19 of those against San Jose's 9.

Fraser Minten opened the scoring at 12:55 of the first, and Jacob Trouba answered with a slap shot just 2:34 later, a goal worth about 1 percent. Charlie McAvoy restored the lead before the period ended. Ivar Stenberg tied it on the power play in the second, but Matthew Poitras tipped one in at 8:42, and Pavel Zacha scored with three seconds left in the period to make it 4-2. Boston's best chances came in that second period, where they held a 2.03 to 1.52 edge in expected goals.

Macklin Celebrini cut it to 4-3 with another power-play goal early in the third, and San Jose pressed. Minten tipped in his second at 11:47, and Will Borgen sealed it at 18:18. Yaroslav Askarov allowed five goals on 3.32 expected, about 1.7 goals worse than average. Jeremy Swayman faced 38 shots and stopped just about what the chances demanded.
